items.summary: Disposition: evidence_needed for fleet-wide security controls; blocked for gated-product public exposure; conditional for ordinary reversible growth that preserves existing consent, disclosures, data handling, claims, and affiliate boundaries. Evidence: fleet-doctor has no run or results; operations deploy, uptime, and error sweeps are unavailable; security sitefacts provide no authentication, access-boundary, secrets, isolation, release-control, dependency, monitoring, incident, or disclosure findings; TLS has no certificates expiring within 30 days but broader TLS posture is unverified; compliance reports 36 pass, 17 fail, and 6 unknown and is not certification. Risk severity: high for gated-product launch because material controls are unknown; medium for bounded reversible fleet changes when no new credentials, dependencies, data collection, permissions, or cross-site behavior are introduced. Exact decision: keep the gated product private, authorize only bounded read-only security evidence capture and already-approved measurement/backlog work, do not create new production security work this cycle, and reassess only when concrete evidence covers authentication/access, secrets, runtime isolation, release/deploy controls, TLS, dependencies/supply chain, data exposure, monitoring/incidents, and security.txt/disclosure readiness. Missing evidence is not a clean bill of health.

Security review accepts the candidate plan's no-new-implementation posture. It does not add a proposal or duplicate active evidence work. Continue existing security evidence capture using authorized metadata and retained artifacts only; do not access credentials or private containers, exploit targets, change permissions, deploy, request duplicate telemetry, or claim certification. The prepared external permissions request remains an owner decision and public launch remains blocked pending all required gates.
